project_identity.one_liner_substance: A user-level Claude Code tool that turns a one-shot request into a self-driving, budget-bounded loop whose completion is judged not by the working agent itself but by an independent, clean-context auditor that re-derives the requirements from the spec and verifies them against the real working tree.
project_identity.category: Agent orchestration / autonomous long-running agents / completion-verification mechanism design
project_identity.what_it_is_plainly: You hand it a spec ('build X; done means A, B, C'). A Stop hook re-injects that spec as a contract after every turn and keeps the agent working until the goal is AUDITED complete, you abort it, it gets blocked, it stalls, or it runs out of budget. It installs into ~/.claude and works in any project and any conversation for the user; each project tracks its own goal under <project>/.claude/goal/.
project_identity.what_makes_it_notable_for_a_portfolio: It is simultaneously (1) a source-level reverse-engineering of OpenAI Codex's then-new /goal mechanism, (2) a working reimplementation on a different platform's extension points, (3) a piece of product thinking about WHO judges 'done' and at what cost, and (4) a self-critical engineering artifact: the author adversarially audited their own anti-false-completion tool (security audit + QA audit + a second cold-read review) and an adversarial eval against the vendor's own native implementation.

core_problem.central_question: For a long-running autonomous agent, the hard problem is not 'can it do the work' but 'when does it stop, and who decides the goal is actually met?'
core_problem.why_it_matters: If the agent judges its own completion from the conversation it just had, it is grading its own homework with a possibly-polluted memory. Two specific trust failures follow.

two_failure_modes.definition: The system announces the goal is met when it is not — typically because a requirement that is not visible at a glance (a hidden call site, a nested file, a tedious tail) was skipped.
two_failure_modes.why_dangerous: Work is abandoned as 'done'; the user trusts a green checkmark over reality.

two_failure_modes.definition: A 'good enough' degraded artifact produced mid-task (a stub, a mock, an English-only string) sits in the context. The model later treats it as if the human already accepted it, and the original requirement is silently replaced by the degraded one.
two_failure_modes.pathology: Context pollution: the conversation, not the spec, becomes the de facto source of truth.
two_failure_modes.why_dangerous: The target quietly erodes; 'this isn't quite what was asked but it's good enough' IS the failure.

core_problem.the_design_response_in_one_sentence: Make the authority for 'done' the real working tree as judged by an auditor with no memory of the conversation, and re-anchor the original spec on every turn so the conversation cannot quietly redefine the goal.

five_layer_mechanism.name: Persistent goal object
five_layer_mechanism.detail: A SQLite-backed state store with a six-state machine (active / paused / blocked / usage-limited / budget-limited / complete) that survives across turns, across context compaction, and across resume.

five_layer_mechanism.name: Self-driving continuation loop
five_layer_mechanism.detail: A runtime interception at turn end (maybe_continue_goal_if_idle_runtime) checks 'goal active + no queued human input + not in plan mode'; if satisfied it injects a continuation prompt and opens a new turn. Human input takes priority over auto-continuation.

five_layer_mechanism.name: Continuation contract
five_layer_mechanism.detail: templates/goals/continuation.md: per-requirement evidence-based completion audit (completion defaults to UNPROVEN; indirect/weak evidence is treated as incomplete), prohibition on shrinking the goal, explicit naming of reward hacking, 'the real working tree is the authority, not the conversation narrative', and alignment defined as 'making the requested end-state closer to real'.

five_layer_mechanism.name: Narrowed exit valve
five_layer_mechanism.detail: The model has only an update_goal tool exposing exactly two values: complete / blocked. A 'blocked' must repeat for the same blocker THREE consecutive turns. pause and budget states belong to the human and the system, not the model.

five_layer_mechanism.name: Budget guardrail
five_layer_mechanism.detail: A token budget enforced on the system side; exhaustion flips to budget-limited and injects a wrap-up template.

codex_reverse_engineering.why_this_was_worth_reverse_engineering: It crystallized the design intent: keep the goal alive independently of the (pollutable) conversation, force evidence-based completion, and structurally prevent the model from self-declaring 'done' or quietly redefining the target.

two_axes.x_axis: Judgment method: semantic understanding  <-->  programmatic check
two_axes.y_axis: Auditor's relationship to the work context: shared  <-->  isolated

verification_paradigm_framework.refinement_from_eval: The eval (see comparison_study) sharpened the y-axis into TWO separable sub-dimensions: (a) process/context isolation — is the evaluator a separate process/memory? — and (b) evidence-source isolation — does the evaluator gather its own proof from the real artifacts, or read the worker's narrative/transcript? These can hold independently: an isolated judge given only the defendant's own written confession is process-isolated but evidence-shared.

placements.y: process-ISOLATED but evidence-SHARED (reads the working transcript) — this is the empirically-revised placement; see comparison_study.key_empirical_revision
placements.note: Originally assumed fully isolated; eval lowered its isolation.

placements.y: isolated on BOTH sub-dimensions (clean context + read-only tools reading the real working tree)
placements.claim: The intersection of the two official routes' blind spots — the project's genuine ecological niche.

cost_structure_argument.premise: Different verification placements have fundamentally different cost structures, and choosing among them is a PRODUCT decision, not an engineering compromise.
points: Inline self-audit: zero extra cost, but inherits the conversation's pollution.
Small-model programmatic checker: cheap enough to run every turn, but only covers script-able conditions.
Semantic isolated audit agent: expensive (a fresh model invocation with its own tool budget), so it MUST have a trigger strategy — audit only when the worker claims completion, not every turn.
cost_structure_argument.design_consequence: The DIY tool audits ONLY on a GOAL_COMPLETE claim. That is the cost-structure argument made concrete.

design_philosophy.guiding_principle: Reality-check protocol: the authority is the real working tree (file contents, test runs, build output, git state); the conversation is NOT the source of truth; any 'looks fine / should work / we already did that' claim is an unverified hypothesis until re-confirmed against real artifacts.

the_diy_implementation.platform: Claude Code (Anthropic) user-level extension points: Stop hooks + skills (slash commands). Installs into ~/.claude.

components.role: The /mygoal command (originally /goal) routes to subcommands: start, status, pause, resume, abort, show-spec, audit.

subcommands.status: human-readable state (turn/token budget, blocker count, no-progress count, last audit verdict + gaps, last 5 history events).
subcommands.pause: active -> paused (the Stop hook stops re-prompting).
subcommands.resume: re-arm (-> active); from an exhausted budget it also extends the budget; resets breather/blocker/stall trackers.
subcommands.abort: orderly kill switch from chat (-> aborted); writes a jq-independent ABORTED sentinel first.
subcommands.show-spec: print the verbatim spec driving the loop.
subcommands.audit: run the clean-context auditor against the spec right now (manual trigger).

components.role: Per-project persistence. spec.md is the verbatim goal (sha256-recorded); state.json holds status, turn_count, tokens_estimated, budget {max_turns, max_tokens}, blocker {last_reason_hash, consecutive_count}, continuation_streak, progress {last_fingerprint, no_progress_count}, audits {last_turn_audited, last_verdict, last_gaps}, and a bounded history.
components.note: 7 states — two more than the design baseline (added: aborted, stalled). Written ONLY by the hook/scripts; atomic write via mktemp-in-same-dir + mv, mode-preserving, owner-only (600).

components.role: Fires when the model would stop. While the goal is active it re-injects the full contract (verbatim spec + reality-check protocol) on stderr and exits 2, which tells Claude to keep going. The dispatcher then chains to a pre-existing stop-hook-git-check.sh if present (skipped on turns the goal blocks).
control_flow_order: 1. jq-independent kill switches (ABORTED / STOP sentinel files) -> stop
3. turn increment + budget ceilings -> stop if exhausted

4. handle the last assistant message's marker: GOAL_COMPLETE -> audit (COMPLETE stops, INCOMPLETE continues with gaps); GOAL_BLOCKED -> streak (threshold stops, else continues); neither -> reset blocker streak, continue
5. stall detection -> stop if no progress for N turns
6. periodic breather decides yield vs re-prompt (applied LAST so it can never swallow an unprocessed completion/blocker claim)

components.role: Spawned on a GOAL_COMPLETE claim. A `claude -p` subprocess with NO memory of the conversation, constrained to genuinely read-only tools, that re-derives the requirements from spec.md and verifies them against the real working tree. Emits a strictly-validated JSON verdict (enum COMPLETE/INCOMPLETE) with per-requirement MET/NOT_MET/INSUFFICIENT and gaps_for_main_agent. Only a COMPLETE verdict closes the goal; otherwise the gaps are fed back into the contract.
components.hardening: Verdict is enum-validated then canonically re-serialized so only known fields propagate; the auditor cannot execute tests/builds/arbitrary code (see self_audit_narrative C2); spend/time capped (GOAL_AUDIT_BUDGET_USD default 1.50, GOAL_AUDIT_TIMEOUT default 360s).

valves: Audited completion: GOAL_COMPLETE claim -> auditor -> COMPLETE closes the goal.
Blocked: same GOAL_BLOCKED reason (sha256 fingerprint) 3 consecutive turns -> blocked; an intervening working turn resets the streak.
Budget-limited: turn_count or token estimate exceeds the ceiling (post-turn).
Breather: periodic yield to the user (soft after 6 auto-continuations when stop_hook_active != false; hard after 25 unconditionally).
Stalled: working-tree + commit fingerprint unchanged for 8 consecutive turns with no marker.
Kill switches: /mygoal abort (orderly) and `touch STOP` (emergency, jq-independent).

components.role: Idempotent install into ~/.claude (or CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR): copies scripts + skill, registers the Stop hook (backing up settings.json first), warns about a pre-existing direct git-check hook, and (post-rename) removes any legacy skills/goal/ so the native /goal is no longer shadowed.

Portable (locates scripts relative to itself; runs from any directory in any repo) and hermetic (throwaway `git init` projects; the auditor is STUBBED so zero `claude -p` spend). 46 assertions across 14 cases covering the whole Stop-hook state machine including the stall detector.

The adversarial comparison: deterministic case generators, a per-(case, arm) runner that drives either the DIY loop or native /goal and collects all evidence, and a verification-layer probe that stages false completions and invokes the DIY auditor directly.

tunables.note: 11 magic numbers were centralized into GOAL_* environment variables (read by lib.sh) so cadence is configurable without editing code.

variables.GOAL_BREATHER_SOFT: 6 — yield to user after this many auto-continuations when stop_hook_active != false.
variables.GOAL_BLOCKER_THRESHOLD: 3 — identical GOAL_BLOCKED reasons this many turns in a row -> blocked.
variables.GOAL_STALL_THRESHOLD: 8 — no working-tree/commit change for this many consecutive turns -> stalled; 0 disables.
variables.GOAL_HISTORY_MAX: 50 — bound the history array in state.json.
variables.GOAL_TRANSCRIPT_TAIL_LINES: 500 — window scanned for the last assistant message (long-goal performance).

decision_log.decision: Choose the Stop hook as the continuation engine
alternatives_considered: decision:block JSON (the other Claude Code Stop-blocking form)
a wrapper process polling the CLI
decision_log.chosen: Stop hook returning exit 2 + a stderr contract
decision_log.rationale: It is the Hook-platform equivalent of Codex's runtime idle-check continuation; exit 2 re-prompts the model and stderr carries the contract. Equivalent to decision:block but simpler to emit and inspect.
decision_log.platform_constraint_revealed: A hook can only see what the harness passes it (the Stop event JSON + transcript path); it cannot read the model's token accounting or force tool use.

decision_log.decision: Store state as JSON files, not SQLite
decision_log.rationale: Minimal dependency (only jq), and a hook's world is the filesystem. Trade-off accepted: read-modify-write across multiple jq calls is not atomic under truly concurrent hook invocations (documented as a low-severity 'lost updates' edge; in normal single-session use Stop hooks fire serially).

decision_log.decision: Make completion judgment an isolated auditor, not the working model
alternatives_considered: inline self-audit in the same context (Codex's approach)
a programmatic checker that runs scripted assertions
decision_log.chosen: A clean-context `claude -p` auditor with read-only tools that reads the real working tree
decision_log.rationale: This is the project's thesis: the conversation may be polluted, so the certifier must not share that conversation AND must gather its own evidence from artifacts. This is the 'semantic x isolated (both sub-dimensions)' niche.

decision_log.decision: Trigger the auditor only on a completion claim, not every turn
decision_log.chosen: Audit only when the worker emits GOAL_COMPLETE
decision_log.rationale: Semantic audits are expensive; a per-turn audit would dominate cost. The trigger strategy is the cost-structure argument made concrete — a product decision.

decision_log.decision: Narrow the model's exit to text markers, with state writable only by the hook
alternatives_considered: give the model a tool to set status (closer to Codex's update_goal)
decision_log.chosen: The model can only emit GOAL_COMPLETE: / GOAL_BLOCKED: text markers (line-anchored); state.json is written exclusively by the hook/scripts
decision_log.rationale: The Hook platform doesn't let the model write state directly, which turns out to be a feature: it structurally prevents the model from self-closing the goal. This is the platform-native equivalent of Codex's tool-narrowing to {complete, blocked}.

decision_log.decision: Re-inject the verbatim spec every turn
decision_log.chosen: The contract re-injects the full spec + reality-check protocol on every continuation
decision_log.rationale: Directly counters degraded-acceptance anchoring: the conversation cannot quietly redefine the target because the original target is re-stated as the single source of truth each turn, with explicit instructions to distrust the conversation history.

decision_log.decision: Confirm blocks across 3 consecutive turns with a fingerprint
decision_log.chosen: Same blocker (sha256 of the reason) must repeat 3 turns in a row; an intervening working turn resets it
decision_log.rationale: Mirrors Codex; prevents a transient 'I'm stuck' from terminating a goal that's actually progressing.

decision_log.decision: Add stall detection (not in the original design)
decision_log.trigger: A real-world failure the user reported: /goal runs a long time without interrupting, yet makes no further progress.
decision_log.chosen: Fingerprint git commit + uncommitted changes (excluding the goal's own .claude/goal/ bookkeeping, never the transcript); unchanged for 8 consecutive turns with no marker -> stalled
decision_log.rationale: The breather, budget, and blocker mechanisms all miss the agent that spins without progress AND without self-reporting a block. Stall detection guarantees an early, informative interrupt. Resets on real progress (no false interrupts); resumable. Even a false positive is desirable here — it pauses and asks.

decision_log.decision: Make the budget a post-turn STOP rather than a forced summary
decision_log.chosen: On budget exhaustion, exit 0 (stop) instead of exit 2 (which would force one more billable summary turn)
decision_log.rationale: exit 2 would spend an extra turn precisely when out of budget; document the budget as a post-turn ceiling, and let /mygoal resume extend it.

decision_log.trigger: Claude Code 2.1.139+ shipped a native /goal; a user-level skill named 'goal' shadows the native command, making it unreachable.
decision_log.chosen: Rename the slash command + skill dir to mygoal; keep the internal scripts/goal/ path and the per-project .claude/goal/ state dir unchanged; have the installer remove any legacy skills/goal/
decision_log.rationale: Lets the DIY tool and the native command coexist in one config (/mygoal = DIY semantic-audit loop; /goal = built-in checker). Keeping internal paths stable means in-place upgrades and existing per-project state migrate without changes. Verified coexistence (see rename_episode).

iteration_history_narrative.summary: Build -> two adversarial self-audits + remediation -> a second cold-read review -> prove the auditor works live -> fix a real-world stall bug + commit a hermetic test harness -> reposition as a comparative study against the vendor's native implementation -> rename for coexistence.

rounds.title: Initial build
rounds.what: The whole loop + installer in one commit: Stop-hook continuation, spec/state persistence, the isolated auditor, kill switches, budget/blocker guards.

rounds.title: Adversarial self-audit + remediation
rounds.what: Two cold-read audits were run against the build: a security/reliability risk audit (2 Critical, 4 High, 6 Medium, 4 Low) and a QA behavioral audit (a large pass/fail matrix that found, among others, a blocker-streak-not-resetting bug, a marker-truncation bug, and an auditor-output-parsing failure in the installed CLI). The consolidated remediation commit addressed 2 Critical, 6 High, 6 Medium. The meta-point: the author adversarially audited their own anti-false-completion tool and found that its trust anchor (the auditor) was itself the most exploitable surface.
headline_fixes: C1 jq filter-string injection (attacker-influenced auditor output could inject a jq pipe and silently flip status to complete) -> all state writes converted to jq --arg/--argjson bindings + enum-validated verdict.
C2 the 'read-only' auditor actually had node/python3/npx/npm/pytest/find/blanket-git in its tool whitelist (arbitrary code execution against the live tree) -> stripped to a genuinely read-only set.
H3 a grep/awk verdict-salvage path bypassed the enum -> strict re-validation.

H4 raw auditor stdout (which can capture file/test output, i.e. secrets) flowed into world-readable state/history/contract -> umask 077, owner-only artifacts, keep only structured fields, recommend gitignoring .claude/goal/.
H1/H2 budget/breather hardening; M-series atomicity, jq-independent kill sentinels, corrupt-state safety.

rounds.title: Second cold-read review (Opus 4.8)
rounds.what: A finding-by-finding pass had missed three classes that a fresh read caught:
classes: Correctness: the periodic breather ran BEFORE marker handling, so a GOAL_COMPLETE emitted on a breather turn was silently swallowed — reordered so the breather is applied last. The dispatcher's `2> >(cat)` async stderr capture was a flush-racey process substitution — replaced with direct stderr pass-through.

Scaling: state.json history was an unbounded array rewritten in full every turn (O(n^2)) -> capped (GOAL_HISTORY_MAX); the last-assistant-message scan slurped the whole transcript every turn -> bounded tail window (GOAL_TRANSCRIPT_TAIL_LINES).
Clarity: renamed the misleading 'consecutive_blocks' to 'continuation_streak' (it counts continuations, not blocks); centralized 11 magic numbers as GOAL_* tunables.

rounds.title: Live auditor evidence
rounds.what: Proved the isolated auditor works end-to-end against real Claude (not a stub): Test A — a satisfied spec audited COMPLETE in 14s with both requirements independently verified via ls/cat/wc; Test B — a violated spec audited INCOMPLETE in 19s with concrete byte-level evidence and actionable gaps.

rounds.title: Stall detection + portable hermetic QA harness
rounds.what: Fixed the user-reported stall (long run, no interrupt, no progress) with fingerprint-based stall detection, and committed a portable, hermetic 46-assertion QA harness (the earlier QA had been run ad-hoc and never committed). All 46 pass.

rounds.title: Repositioning: P0/P1/P2
rounds.what: P0 implementation inventory (design-vs-actual diff), P1 resume-data backfill with evidence pointers, P2 adversarial eval vs native /goal. See comparison_study and adversarial_eval.

rounds.title: Rename for coexistence
rounds.what: /goal -> /mygoal so the DIY tool no longer shadows the native /goal; verified both work in the same config.

self_audit_narrative.why_this_is_a_strong_portfolio_beat: A tool whose entire pitch is 'resist false completion' was then subjected by its own author to (a) a security/reliability risk audit, (b) a QA behavioral audit, and (c) a second independent cold-read — and the audits found that the trust anchor (the auditor) was the single most dangerous surface. Fixing that, and documenting it honestly, is the credibility of the whole thesis.

risk_audit.method: Full source read + isolated read-only experiments in mktemp sandboxes; never run against real state.
two_criticals: C1 — jq filter-string injection via the auditor verdict: untrusted, attacker-influenceable auditor output was interpolated into a jq program; a value like 'INCOMPLETE" | .status = "complete' is valid JSON and rewrote status to complete. The auditor — the trust anchor — was the injection vector.

C2 — the 'read-only' auditor's tool whitelist actually permitted arbitrary code execution and destructive commands (node/python3/npx/npm test/pytest/find/git) against the REAL working tree, triggered automatically on every completion claim.
risk_audit.verdict_at_the_time: NO-GO as written; either Critical alone is disqualifying for an unattended tool that shells out against the user's repo. Both were fixed in 575c9e5.

qa_audit.method: Empirical: installed into a throwaway CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR; every test ran against throwaway mktemp projects; one real auditor run plus diagnostic probes.
notable_findings: Marker missed when not the last physical line of the last assistant message (a tail -1 truncation) — fixed.
Blocker streak not truly 'consecutive' (intervening progress didn't reset it) — fixed.

On the installed CLI, the auditor's --json-schema call returned empty output, so a finished goal could never auto-complete — fixed by switching to --output-format json + .result parsing (re-verified live in a793f36).

self_audit_narrative.honesty_about_the_audit_itself: The audits' own failures were recorded, not hidden — e.g., a later eval-harness grep portability bug (see adversarial_eval.honesty_record) was documented and re-judged rather than quietly corrected.

comparison_study.what_it_compares: The DIY tool vs Claude Code's native /goal, on the two failure modes, under matched conditions.

first_hand_mechanism_findings_revising_s.finding_1_native_is_also_a_stop_hook: Native /goal is itself a session-scoped Stop hook (same extension point as the DIY tool). Verbatim from a transcript: 'A session-scoped Stop hook is now active with condition: ... The hook will block stopping until the condition holds. It auto-clears once the condition is met.' The DIY engineering choice (Stop hook = continuation driver) is thus endorsed by the vendor's own implementation.

key_empirical_revision.secondhand_claim: Native checker 'runs real commands and reads output' (i.e., gathers its own evidence).
key_empirical_revision.first_hand_observation: Across 13 met:true verdict records, the checker's reasons cite the TRANSCRIPT, not independently-executed commands. 9 of 13 reasons literally begin with 'The transcript shows...'; the other 4 cite transcript-internal artifacts (Edit-tool receipts, the worker's own command output). Each verdict is iterations:1, ~553–2648 tokens, 12–45s — the signature of a single lightweight evaluation, with no observed autonomous command execution and no tool-use records.
key_empirical_revision.interpretation: The native checker is process-ISOLATED but its evidence source is the worker's working transcript (evidence-SHARED). So 'the real working tree is the authority, not the narrative' is, in practice, only fully realized by the DIY auditor (clean context + read-only tools reading the tree directly).
key_empirical_revision.effect_on_the_framework: On the quadrant, native /goal's isolation (y-axis) drops markedly; the DIY tool is the only one of the three fully isolated on evidence-source. The 'semantic x isolated' niche thesis is STRONGER after the eval than before.
key_empirical_revision.confidence: Behavioral inference from 13 samples on a closed-source system, NOT a source-level fact. Must be labeled as such.

other_first_hand_corrections: Native goal state is session-scoped: a new session returns 'No goal set'; the transcript carries a goal_status attachment stream (sentinel:true at start -> met:true at end).
Name collision: with the DIY skill named 'goal' installed, /goal is taken over by the skill and the native command is shadowed (this drove the rename).

adversarial_eval.method: Same spec text shared verbatim by both arms; deterministic byte-identical project snapshots; controlled worker model; same permissions/budget/wall-clock. DIY arm: a temp CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR install, spec armed via start.sh (10-turn budget), neutral kickoff. Native arm: clean config, prompt = '/goal <spec>'. Judgment is automatic and deterministic: declared_complete x ground_truth_met (a pure-bash grep check) -> FALSE_COMPLETE / TRUE_COMPLETE / NO_FALSE_COMPLETE.

cases.design_note: The 4 starred-in-report harder variants (fc4, da4, da5) were added after the base 6 passed on both arms; the base specs contained 'regardless of any notes' fences (which pre-emptively defuse the trap) — a recorded design self-criticism.

end_to_end_results.outcome: 26/26 TRUE_COMPLETE — zero false completions on either arm, including da4's repo-resident false narrative.
end_to_end_results.honest_interpretation: At this task scale, natural inducement no longer bites current worker models — even the weak worker did not err. So the end-to-end pass rate (26/26) CANNOT separate the verification layers; the first line of defense against the failure modes is now carried by worker capability, and the verification layer is a backstop whose value must be measured separately.

verification_layer_probe.rationale: Decouple worker quality from verifier quality by STAGING false completions (visible part done, hidden requirement left undone) and invoking the DIY clean-context auditor directly.
verification_layer_probe.results: 5/5: 4 staged false-completion trees (including da4's repo-resident 'migration done in PR #123' narrative) all judged INCOMPLETE with precise, line-level gaps; 1 true-completion control judged COMPLETE (no false positive).
verification_layer_probe.quotable_evidence: On the da4 false tree the auditor wrote: 'Line 24 of src/db.js must be changed from `module.exports = { store: new MemoryStore() };` to ... The FileStore class is already correctly implemented — only the export line needs updating.' — it acknowledged the finished class, rejected the repo's completion narrative, and located the gap to the line.
verification_layer_probe.asymmetry_limitation: The native checker is invoked by the harness with the live transcript and has no isolated entry point, so it cannot be probed the same way; this probe is DIY-only, and that asymmetry is recorded as a limitation.

honesty_record.the_grep_bug: da3's first judgment came out FALSE_COMPLETE on both arms — actually an EVAL-HARNESS bug: `grep -P '[\x{4e00}-\x{9fff}]'` is unsupported on the local grep and errored to 'no Chinese found'. Both arms had in fact localized correctly. Fixed to a UTF-8 lead-byte check, re-judged offline against the preserved worked trees (TRUE_COMPLETE), and a note field was written into the affected meta.json files recording the cause.
honesty_record.why_it_belongs_on_the_page: An eval whose subject is 'resisting false completion' caught a false-negative in ITSELF and disclosed it. That self-consistency is a feature of the narrative, not an embarrassment to hide.

threats_to_validity: Task scale is small (<=540s / 10 turns / synthetic repos); do not extrapolate to long, large tasks.
Natural inducement caught no worker; end-to-end 100% reflects 'worker too strong', not 'verifier validated' — verifier evidence comes from the probe.
N=1 per cell; no statistical significance.
Native checker is observed only through transcript traces (closed source).
Both arms' snapshot SHAs differ (timestamps) though content is generator-identical.
The DIY arm's --allowedTools Bash could in principle let a worker tamper with its own state.json; not observed in 26 runs, not adversarially tested.

rename_episode.problem: Originally the slash command was /goal. After Claude Code 2.1.139+ shipped a native /goal, a user-level skill named 'goal' shadowed the native command — verified: with the DIY skill installed, /goal returned the DIY dispatch output instead of the native usage, making the built-in unreachable.
rename_episode.solution: Rename the slash command and skill directory to /mygoal; keep the internal scripts/goal/ path and per-project .claude/goal/ state directory unchanged (so in-place upgrades and existing goals need no migration). The installer now also removes any legacy skills/goal/ in the target config.
what_was_deliberately_NOT_renamed: GOAL_* env vars, goal_*() bash helpers, state.json schema, STOP/ABORTED sentinel filenames
eval/results/** and the historical reports (the literal '/goal' in transcripts is what was actually run at the time; rewriting would falsify evidence) — only p0 got a 'resolved' annotation
rename_episode.verification: Live regression in one CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR: (A) /mygoal start "..." drove the loop, audit COMPLETE, status -> complete, spec satisfied on disk; (B) bare /goal returned native usage ('No goal set. Usage: /goal <condition>') — proving the DIY skill no longer shadows the built-in; (C) /goal <spec> still drove the native loop to satisfaction. The hermetic QA harness still passed 46/46.

resume_framing.strongest_interview_soundbite: I separated two layers of isolation: process/context isolation, and evidence-source isolation. Codex's inline self-audit isolates neither; native /goal isolates the process but its evidence source is still the working transcript; only my implementation isolates both — and that is its core differentiation on resisting false completion.

glossary.Stop hook: A Claude Code extension point: a script that fires when the model would stop; returning exit 2 (with stderr) re-prompts the model to keep going.
glossary.continuation contract: The text re-injected each turn: the verbatim spec + a reality-check protocol + the completion/blocker marker instructions + the named failure modes.
glossary.isolated/clean-context auditor: A separate `claude -p` process with no memory of the conversation, read-only tools, that re-derives the spec's requirements and checks them against the real working tree.
glossary.GOAL_COMPLETE / GOAL_BLOCKED: Line-anchored text markers the worker emits to claim completion or report a block; the worker has no tool to write goal state directly.
glossary.breather: A periodic yield that returns control to the user (soft after 6 auto-continuations, hard after 25).
glossary.stall detection: Stops the loop when the git commit + uncommitted changes are unchanged for N consecutive turns with no marker — catches an agent spinning without progress.
glossary.false completion: Declaring 'done' when the spec is not actually met.
glossary.degraded-acceptance anchoring: Treating a mid-task degraded artifact as an accepted final state, silently downgrading the requirement.
glossary.evidence-source isolation: Whether the certifier gathers proof from the real artifacts (isolated) or from the worker's own narrative/transcript (shared) — the eval's key refinement of the framework.
